evidence.claim: A planned desert town meets dunes made from volcanic ash and pumice.
evidence.quote: The dunes are composed mostly of ash and pumice from the eruption of Mount Mazama

evidence.claim: A planned desert town
evidence.quote: Real estate development around a planned community by M. Penn Phillips, called Christmas Valley, started after World War II.

evidence.claim: The Christmas Valley Back Country Byway runs 93 miles into Oregon’s high desert.
evidence.quote: the 93-mile-long Christmas Valley Back Country Byway provides access to breathtaking high desert landscapes and unique geological features.

evidence.claim: The Bureau of Land Management presents the route as a way to reach geological features, from dunes of volcanic ash and pumice to an eroded volcano.
evidence.quote: From off-highway vehicle use on dunes composed largely of ash and pumice that blew into the area 7,000 years ago when Mt. Mazama erupted to hiking in the remains of an eroded volcano

evidence.claim: The Black Hills Interpretive Site offers a parking area and an interpretive sign, reached on foot or by four-wheel-drive vehicle.
evidence.quote: Accessible by foot or 4WD vehicle, it includes a parking area, fencing, and an interpretive sign.

evidence.claim: The Black Hills Interpretive Site
evidence.quote: The Black Hills Interpretive Site is a popular starting point for day hiking and photography.

evidence.claim: The settlement along the way took shape as a planned community after World War II.
evidence.quote: Real estate development around a planned community by M. Penn Phillips, called Christmas Valley, started after World War II.

evidence.claim: In 1961, developer M. Penn Phillips laid out Christmas Valley with holiday street names, an airport, a water system and an artificial lake.
evidence.quote: In 1961, developer M. Penn Phillips laid out the townsite, including its fanciful holiday street names (such as Candy Lane, Mistletoe Road, Comet Street, Vixen Street, etc.), the Christmas Valley Airport, a water system, a golf course, a lodge, rodeo grounds, and an artificial lake

evidence.claim: He marketed the land to prospective farmers and retirees in California, offering bus tours and flights.
evidence.quote: Phillips aggressively promoted the community in California to young, would-be farmers and retirees; often providing free bus tours and flights

evidence.claim: The parcels sold quickly, but few buyers moved there.
evidence.quote: The company quickly sold out the parcels, though despite Phillips' claims that the community would soon have more than 5,000 residents, few actually moved there.

evidence.claim: The holiday theme had an older naming history behind it: Christmas was a corruption of Christman, the name of stockman Peter Christman, who grazed cattle in the area.
evidence.quote: Christmas Lake, Christmas (Lake) Valley, and nearby Peter's Sink and Peter's Creek were named for pioneer stockman Peter Christman, who grazed his cattle there

evidence.claim: Christmas was a corruption of Christman
evidence.quote: The name "Christmas" was an early corruption of the name Christman that became entrenched in the vernacular by 1900.

evidence.claim: The byway begins at Oregon 31 and County Road 5-10.
evidence.quote: The Byway start at the intersection of Hwy 31 and County Road 5-10.

evidence.claim: Christmas Valley provides a town anchor before the dunes to its east.
evidence.quote: public lands east of Christmas Valley in Lake County, Oregon

evidence.claim: Beyond the dunes lies Lost Forest Research Natural Area; Fossil Lake lies to their west.
evidence.quote: the Lost Forest Research Natural Area, east of the dunes as well as the land around nearby Fossil Lake to the west

evidence.claim: The dunes themselves reach 60 feet high, built largely from the eruption that formed Crater Lake.
evidence.quote: The dunes are up to 60 feet (18 m) high.

evidence.claim: built largely from the eruption that formed Crater Lake
evidence.quote: The dunes are composed mostly of ash and pumice from the eruption of Mount Mazama that formed Crater Lake 7,000 years ago.

evidence.claim: Candy Lane and Mistletoe Road were part of M. Penn Phillips’s 1961 plan for Christmas Valley.
evidence.quote: In 1961, developer M. Penn Phillips laid out the townsite, including its fanciful holiday street names (such as Candy Lane, Mistletoe Road

evidence.claim: The townsite also included an airport, golf course and artificial lake.
evidence.quote: the Christmas Valley Airport, a water system, a golf course, a lodge, rodeo grounds, and an artificial lake

evidence.claim: Phillips sold California buyers the prospect of readily farmed land, but few took up residence.
evidence.quote: marketing the potential of the land as green and readily farmed.  The company quickly sold out the parcels, though despite Phillips' claims that the community would soon have more than 5,000 residents, few actually moved there.

evidence.claim: The community is now largely devoted to alfalfa farming.
evidence.quote: Christmas Valley is largely an alfalfa farming community.

evidence.claim: Its lake, originally Christmas Valley Lake, is called Baert Lake.
evidence.quote: an artificial lake originally named Christmas Valley Lake and now called Baert Lake.

evidence.claim: Baert Lake is artificial, with part of its shoreline bordering the golf course. The Christmas Valley Park and Recreation District manages it, keeping one element of the planned town in recreational use.
evidence.quote: Baert Lake is a small artificial lake in the unincorporated community of Christmas Valley in the U.S. state of Oregon. Managed by the Christmas Valley Park and Recreation District, the lake is used for fishing, boating, and swimming

evidence.claim: with part of its shoreline bordering the golf course
evidence.quote: Part of the lake borders the Christmas Valley Golf Course.

evidence.claim: Crack in the Ground marks the western edge of a depression formed when older rock sank during eruptions from Four Craters Lava Field.
evidence.quote: The eruptions from the Four Craters Lava Field were accompanied by a slight sinking of the older rock surface, forming a shallow, graben-like structure about 2 miles (3.2 km) wide and extending to the south into an old lake basin. Crack in the Ground marks the western edge of this small, volcano-tectonic depression.

evidence.claim: The volcanic fissure extends about two miles, with depths nearly 30 feet below ground level.
evidence.quote:
Crack in the Ground is a volcanic fissure about 2 miles (3.2 km) long
 with depths measuring nearly 30 feet (9 m) below ground level

evidence.claim: It lies at the lava field’s southwest corner.
evidence.quote: The fissure is located at the southwest corner of Four Craters Lava Field.

evidence.claim: These dunes owe much of their material to Mount Mazama, the volcano whose eruption formed Crater Lake.
evidence.quote: The dunes are composed mostly of ash and pumice from the eruption of Mount Mazama that formed Crater Lake 7,000 years ago.

evidence.claim: Wind carried ash and pumice into this area 7,000 years ago.
evidence.quote: dunes composed largely of ash and pumice that blew into the area 7,000 years ago when Mt. Mazama erupted

evidence.claim: The dune complex covers 11,000 acres of public land and reaches heights of 60 feet.
evidence.quote: The Christmas Valley Sand Dunes are a natural sand dune complex covering 11,000 acres

evidence.claim: In 1983, the Bureau of Land Management combined the dunes, Lost Forest Research Natural Area and Fossil Lake into one Area of Critical Environmental Concern.
evidence.quote: In 1983, the Bureau of Land Management joined the Christmas Valley Sand Dunes, Lost Forest Research Natural Area, and Fossil Lake into a single Area of Critical Environmental Concern.

evidence.claim: That shared management area encompasses contrasting neighbors: Fossil Lake west of the dunes and Lost Forest to the east. The Bureau of Land Management administers all three.
evidence.quote: The Christmas Valley Sand Dunes area is administered by Bureau of Land Management.  The Bureau of Land Management also oversees the Lost Forest Research Natural Area, east of the dunes as well as the land around nearby Fossil Lake to the west

evidence.claim: The dunes reach heights of 60 feet.
evidence.quote: The dunes are up to 60 feet (18 m) high.
